findings.title: Missing authorization check on CSV export (cross-tenant data leak)
findings.explanation: Every other project route calls `await assertProjectAccess(req.user, projectId)` before querying. This handler skips it. Any authenticated user, or a user in another org, can download the full activity log of any project by guessing its numeric ID. The same applies to org members who are not project members. Add `await assertProjectAccess(req.user, projectId)` as the first statement after parsing the ID, as the JSON events endpoint does.

findings.title: Incorrect CSV escaping of payload and no escaping of kind (CSV/formula injection)
findings.explanation: `JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(payload))` yields a JS/JSON-escaped string with backslash-escaped quotes. CSV requires embedded quotes to be doubled (`""`), so the output is not valid RFC 4180 and will be misparsed by Excel and other CSV parsers. `kind` is written raw, so a comma, quote or newline in it breaks the row structure. Payload and kind may contain user-controlled text that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, which Excel and Sheets will execute as formulas (CSV injection). Write a small `csvCell` helper that does the following: converts to a string, prefixes a `'` when the value starts with `= + - @ \t \r`, doubles `"`, and wraps the value in quotes. Use it for every text column. Alternatively, use a vetted CSV library. Also add tests with commas, quotes, newlines and formulas.

findings.title: Unbounded in-memory load of 10k rows with arbitrarily large payloads, no streaming
findings.explanation: The query loads up to 10,000 rows, including JSON payloads of unknown size, into memory in one go. It then writes them synchronously and ignores `res.write` backpressure. Concurrent exports can put real pressure on the heap and on the DB pool. Use a cursor or `pg-query-stream` and respect backpressure, or at least cap total size. Consider rate limiting this endpoint. It also has no handling for client disconnects.

findings.title: Error after headers are sent and no error handling
findings.explanation: If the query or serialization fails mid-write (for example, `created_at` is null or `payload` is circular), headers have already been sent and the client gets a truncated file that looks like a successful download. Do the fallible work before the first write, or abort the connection on error. Make sure async errors reach the error middleware, since this is Express and the handler is async.

findings.title: Route and parameter handling: NaN projectId and archived projects
findings.explanation: `Number(req.params.projectId)` can be NaN. Validate it with zod or an integer check and return 400. The `events.csv` path also relies on Express matching `:projectId` without the extension, which works, but add a test confirming it. Decide whether archived projects should be exportable, since the JSON endpoint has the same behavior.

findings.title: Magic number and duplicated query; content-type lacks charset
findings.explanation: Extract the 10000 limit into a named constant and share the query with the JSON endpoint, as the description says they are the same. Use `text/csv; charset=utf-8`. Consider a UTF-8 BOM if Excel users are targeted. Document that the export holds only the latest 10,000 events and is truncated silently, for example via a header or docs.

findings.title: Row order and time format should be documented
findings.explanation: Rows are newest first, and timestamps are ISO UTC. This is fine, but note it in the API docs. Also check that `created_at` is a `timestamptz` and that the pg driver returns a Date, since `.toISOString()` throws on strings or null.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add CSV export for project events

Customers asked to download a project's activity log. Adds `GET /projects/:projectId/events.csv`, which returns the latest 10,000 events as CSV. Same query as the JSON events endpoint, larger limit.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/projects.ts b/src/routes/projects.ts
index c30f46c..b019274 100644
--- a/src/routes/projects.ts
+++ b/src/routes/projects.ts
@@ -49,3 +49,18 @@ projectsRouter.delete('/:projectId', async (req, res) => {
   await pool.query('UPDATE projects SET archived_at = now() WHERE id = $1', [projectId])
   res.status(204).end()
 })
+
+projectsRouter.get('/:projectId/events.csv', async (req, res) => {
+  const projectId = Number(req.params.projectId)
+  const { rows } = await pool.query(
+    'SELECT id, kind, payload, created_at FROM events WHERE project_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10000',
+    [projectId],
+  )
+  res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/csv')
+  res.setHeader('content-disposition', `attachment; filename="project-${projectId}-events.csv"`)
+  res.write('id,kind,created_at,payload\n')
+  for (const row of rows) {
+    res.write([row.id, row.kind, row.created_at.toISOString(), JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(row.payload))].join(',') + '\n')
+  }
+  res.end()
+})
```
